text:
sara: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete plan for runtime precision downgrades (FP8 -> INT8 -> 4-bit) when GPU pressure spikes. How do we guarantee we don't silently regress quality for important routes?

mike: Agree this is urgent. My take: two-tier safety: 1) offline regression gates per profile, 2) runtime escrow + soft-hysteresis.

claire: Can you sketch the "escrow" idea? never seen that term used here. :thinking:

mike: Escrow = store a small set of golden prompts + expected scoring signals for each route/model. At runtime if we consider lowering precision, evaluate a tiny sample (1-3 prompts) against quantized path and compare score delta to threshold. If delta > budget -> block downgrade.

izzy: That sounds expensive if done per-request. Proposal: do escrow checks only on policy transitions and periodically (every N mins) while downgraded. For overload fast-path, allow temporary degrade for X seconds before running escrow check asynchronously and revert if fail.

sara: Good. We should also define signals: token-level logprobs? LM-Score? embedding-similarity between outputs? We need a single numeric signal for policy.

mike: Minimal signal: semantic-similarity on final answer embedding (cosine) + perplexity delta. Weighted sum. Example: score = 0.7*cosine + 0.3*normed_perp_delta. Threshold tuned per route.

claire: Add a lightweight deterministic check to ensure critical tokens (markers/keys) don't mutate. e.g., exact-match on extraction fields. For structured outputs, require schema match.

izzy: Also consider KV-cache compatibility — switching precision mid-conversation can corrupt caches. We should either drop cache on precision switch or maintain homogeneous cache lanes.

sara: Agreed. Implementation notes: - cache lane label on request -> if precision changes, invalidate or route to a different runtime. - annotate traces with precision_profile_id.

mike: We need a small metadata contract for precision profiles. Proposed JSON:

```
{
  "profile_id": "q_fp8_v2",
  "supported_ops": ["attn", "ffn"],
  "quality_estimates": {"sem_sim": "0.992", "perp_factor": "1.05"},
  "canary_prompts": ["prompt_hash_1", "prompt_hash_2"],
  "fallback_targets": ["q_int8_v3", "q_4bit_safe"]
}
```

We should store profile-level offline stats and attach a monotonic degradation score.

claire: Where do we keep the thresholds? Route-level config in the control plane tied to SLOs. E.g., route /billing-chat has tighter thresholds than /notes-digest.

izzy: Rollout/CICD: when we ship a new quant profile, require: unit tests (operators), offline eval diff < epsilon, canary on 0.5% traffic with escrow on, then promote. Document rollback triggers.

sara: Ops playbook snippet for oncall:

- If high queue + automatic downgrade -> check escrow-dashboard for failing prompts.
- If > 3 failing escrow checks in 10m, trigger auto-rollback to previous profile.
- If KV-cache mismatch errors spike, roll back immediately.

mike: One more tradeoff: latency vs sample size. Smaller escrow sample reduces safety. I'll add exponential backoff for sample size: start 1 prompt, if pass, keep. If we see drift signals in telemetry, bump to 3 and run offline eval.

claire: For compatibility with Dedicated/Private customers, expose a knob: enforce_profile_pin: boolean. If true, runtime will never downgrade for that customer.

izzy: Can we avoid shipping PII in canary prompts? Use synthetic probes and hashed prompt IDs. Store cleartext only in encrypted vault for audit.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/precision-escrow-checks -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) by izzy at 1766668200

sara: Action items: @mike draft a short RFC addendum (escrow semantics + profile metadata schema). @izzy write the canary playbook steps and KV-cache lane spec. @claire propose the default thresholds for three sensitivity tiers. I'll own the telemetry dashboard for escrow failures.

mike: Will do today.

izzy: Taking the canary playbook. Will include commands and example k8s annotations.

claire: I'll start with thresholds: strict/standard/lenient and share numbers.

sara: Thanks team — let's avoid silent quality regressions. :thumbsup:
